commits.edited_message:
OT: Cache first-input classes per contextual RuleSet (#6234)

Build a compact class digest for every format-2 contextual RuleSet in
the subtable's existing external cache.  Reject a RuleSet before walking
its rules when the next input glyph cannot match any rule's first class.

Rules without another input position force the digest open.  Digest
collisions only cause the normal rule walk, and allocation failure falls
back to the uncached path.

Both format-2 subtables size their digest arrays through one shared
count helper.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

[gsubgpos] Preserve concat hazards at end of input (#6238)

The RuleSet fast paths filtered out rules requiring another glyph when
the skipping iterator reached the end of the buffer. Unlike the normal
rule walk, that early return did not record the resulting
unsafe-to-concat range.

Keep the end-of-input optimization, but track filtered rules and mark
their concat hazard before returning. Cover both contextual and chained
contextual rule sets with a five-rule font that forces the fast paths.

Also cap the per-RuleSet digest precompute of the format-2 contextual
subtables at HB_CACHED_RULE_SET_COUNT entries, so fonts with
pathological class counts no longer precompute unbounded digests at
face load; rule sets past the cap keep the uncached rule walk.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: The defect is split between the digest machinery of ContextFormat2_5/ChainContextFormat2_5 and is only reachable when both edited commits combine. Commit 3c6e57fcb ("OT: Cache first-input classes per contextual RuleSet") introduces the per-RuleSet digest cache: external_cache_create() sizes the rule_sets[] flexible array as `count = ruleSet.len` and fills exactly that many digests, while _apply() later resolves a digest with `cache && index < ruleSet.len ? &cache->rule_sets[index] : nullptr` where `index` is the font-controlled ClassDef class of the input glyph. The edit to this commit is a pure behavior-preserving refactor: both allocation sites now call a shared identity helper cached_rule_set_count(n) = n, so the invariant 'allocation covers every index the guard admits' still holds and the commit is benign on its own (verified: the PoC runs clean on this commit's rewritten tree). Commit a43cefa11 ("[gsubgpos] Preserve concat hazards at end of input", a later commit in the same file) edits only the helper body, capping it: cached_rule_set_count(n) = hb_min(n, HB_CACHED_RULE_SET_COUNT) with the cap motivated as bounding face-load precompute. Read alone, that diff is self-consistent: it changes one function, and its message claims rule sets past the cap 'keep the uncached rule walk'. But the guard in _apply(), introduced by the first commit and untouched by the second, still admits every index in [0, ruleSet.len), so for any contextual subtable with ruleSetCount > 512 whose ClassDef maps a covered glyph to a class >= 512, _apply hands RuleSet::apply a digest pointer past the end of the truncated allocation, and the >4-rules fast path dereferences it in digest->may_have() -- a heap out-of-bounds read (READ of size 8, 2304 bytes past a 4352-byte block under ASan). Neither commit's diff alone contains a mismatch: the first keeps allocation == admitted range (identity helper), and the second never touches the guard or the raw cache indexing, so a commit-by-commit reviewer sees correct maintenance in each. A correct fix must reconcile the two sides across commits: bounding the allocation in the helper requires also bounding the guard (or the fast-path digest use) to the cached count -- code introduced in the other commit. Fixing only commit a43cefa11's diff (any cap value, or reverting the helper body alone) still leaves the guard admitting uncached indices whenever a cap exists at all, and fixing only commit 3c6e57fcb's diff (the guard/allocation code) cannot know the cap semantics that the later commit introduces; the bug is only removed by a change that makes the admitted index range and the cached rule-set count agree, which spans both commits.
